There is a sharp contrast between the two pictures. In the left, one father enjoys watching TV, yet he urges his son to study hard; in the right, another father and his son study together at desks. The caption below the pictures implies that example is better than precept.

The distinct actions of the two fathers symbolize different examples, and examples are critical to the formation of the children’s view of life. Actually, examples are “silent language”, which can enlighten kids by setting models. Good examples can help children establish ambitious life goals, overcome obstacles and then achieve a meaningful life. Take Madame Curie for example. She served as a good model for her daughter Irène with her curiosity about knowledge and perseverance in belief, which helped Irène win her own Nobel Prize. On the contrary, bad examples fail to instruct children how to love and how to be self-confident, and cannot help them foster good communication and social skills. Children are more likely to imitate models than listen to admonitions, so parents’ actions are quite more influential to children compared with verbal guidance and admonition. Additionally, if parents are saying one thing and doing another, how can they ask their children to do the right things?

Apparently, parental examples not only affect children’s behavior, but shape their characters. Therefore, parents should pay special attention to parental model, practice what they preach to set good examples and impact children imperceptibly, so that children will gradually accept and truly take these examples as guidelines.

A simple life philosophy lies behind it, “United we stand, divided we fall.” In other words, cooperation is the best policy in the face of challenges. Take Tu Youyou for example. In cooperation with colleagues, Tu Youyou discovered a novel therapy against malaria. She won the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for the remarkable achievement. Likewise, the Chinese government and its people together defeated SARS in 2003. These examples indicate that things differ greatly with cooperation. It can enable us to acquire collective achievements and ultimate success.

The potential benefits of cooperation are clear. The resources, such as databases, strategies and social connections, could be shared through cooperation, which can create more value and improve resource utilization. So cooperation must be rooted in us—in the lives we lead, the work we share, and even the competitions we participate in.

Dear Sir or Madam/Librarian,

As a regular library user, I am thankful for your excellent service. I have benefited a great deal from it. Nevertheless, I believe that the following suggestions are beneficial to the further improvement of the library.

The primary task is to establish a network platform which can provide teaching courseware and materials. Through the platform, students can search for any available references. At the same time, in the information age, the absence of electronic reading rooms may not be condemned, but their presence is a definite sign of improvement. Additionally, self-checkout machines can provide much convenience.

I hope you will seriously consider my suggestions. Looking forward to your reply.

Yours faithfully,
Li Ming

items.referenceEssay:
The drawing depicts a scene from a football match. In the game, the goalkeeper sees himself as a dwarf, while the attacker views the same goalkeeper as a big giant. This difference stems from the goalkeeper thinking he’s not good enough and the attacker thinking his opponent is too powerful. The drawing implies that people often think challenges more difficult than they really are.

Our thoughts can change how we act and what happens to us. The goalkeeper and the attacker in the drawing are good examples. The goalkeeper's negative thoughts may stop him from doing his best, while the attacker's fear of the challenge may lead him to miss a really good chance. But if they believe in themselves and regard the challenge as something they can handle, they may perform better.

Therefore, we need to learn to see ourselves in the right way when confronted with challenges. With the right mindset, we can overcome challenges and do better than we thought we could. After all, what truly traps us is not the difficulty itself, but our own negative imagination.
